finding: Corn oil is a comparator in a mouse toxicology design. The abstract supplies no culinary oil or human rigidity result.
An isocaloric corn-oil diet is one of three exposures in a colitis mouse experiment. Its measured cytokine results do not establish Parkinson rigidity.
Corn oil is an injected solvent control in a mouse motor and neurotoxicity study. Rotarod time is not a rigidity outcome or a refined oil ingestion comparison.
The neonatal case concerns genetic parkinsonian-pyramidal syndrome. Feeding support is incidental to the diagnosis and no oil contrast is presented.
Tube feeding is an access category in a retrospective medication-timing preprint. No feed formula, corn-oil comparison or rigidity result is estimated.
The retrospective comparison concerns adverse events of intestinal levodopa gel. Enteral nutrition co-occurs in several MSA patients without an oil-specific motor outcome.
The reported case concerns recurrent fever during overlapping levodopa and feeding. No specified refined corn oil or individual rigidity response is given.
The outcome is a gastrostomy complication in series with intestinal drug infusion or nutrition. The abstract gives no corn-oil rigidity comparison.
The clinical context is tube feeding and intestinal gel use in advanced Parkinson disease. The abstract does not identify refined corn oil or a separate rigidity estimate.
Tube feeding is an event in a Parkinson cohort analysis. The abstract supplies no feeding-oil composition or symptom response attributed to oil.
Nicotine and enteral nutrition are studied for levodopa pharmacokinetics in healthy participants and cell assays. Clinical rigidity and isolated oil effects are unreported.
Existing Parkinson rigidity case changed feeding formulation, protein, feeding schedule and medication timing together. Historical corn-oil listings do not isolate an effect.
Existing separate case reports a probable protein and levodopa interaction. The accessible abstract leaves formula and corn-oil identity unresolved.
Feeding-associated rigidity is described in a child with dopa-responsive dystonia. No corn-oil assignment or Parkinson comparison was reported.
